- When sentiment is predominantly bullish (≥ 0.67) and model forecasts are rising steadily, reduce forecast slope if true outcome shows early correction or mean reversion.
- If model forecasts overshoot a recent spike (e.g., >85.5) and sentiment is neutral or bearish, cap upward momentum and adjust downward by 1–2% per event horizon.
- In high-event periods (≥20 events/30d) with net supply negative, model should not over-forecast upward unless sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.80) and recent prices are volatile.
- If true outcome dips sharply after a forecast peak, apply “lag correction” — reduce next forecast by 0.5–1.5% for each subsequent day if sentiment remains neutral or bearish.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >1.5σ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 0.3–0.7% per day until convergence with true trend.
- In low-sentiment (≤0.33) or bearish sentiment (≤0.50) environments, avoid upward forecasts unless recent price is >82.0 and volatility is high (σ > 1.2).
